outcomes: A TypeScript program reads Putnami CLI machine output as typed documents instead of untyped JSON
An invalid document is reported as a list of exact violations rather than as a missing field several frames later
This reader and the Go reader agree, because both execute the same committed conformance corpus
A document recorded by an older CLI build stays readable
nonGoals: Owning the CLI machine contract, which belongs to the protocols/cli module
Running the CLI or selecting which producer events it emits
Promising that a pre-1.0 minor release keeps the previous binding surface

requirements.text: Session placement is optional for older records. When present it records both requested and actual execution as local or remote, including a remote request executed locally; malformed values are rejected without changing the session tree identity.

TypeScript and Go validate the same workload-qualification contract and verdict corpus and emit the same qualify.* codes: unknown or case-aliased members, a state outside the closed vocabulary, and a passed verdict without every phase and request passed, a matching sha and a clean teardown are refused. Both compute the same contract digest bytes.

TypeScript and Go parse the same session-reporter chunk and ACK corpus, verify the bounded base64 payload and SHA-256 digest, and match every per-artifact sequence/offset identity field without introducing a second session result shape.
A machine document is version 2 exactly when it carries protocolVersion 2; a document without the field is version 1, and the version-1 envelope stays exported for reading recorded output.
Validating each fixture of the committed conformance corpus produces exactly the violation set the corpus pins, and the corpus covers every document kind and every violation code.
Every exported document type's member set is asserted field-by-field against the published JSON schema, so a schema change that this binding has not followed fails a test.
The report bounds, the machine-output budgets and the test-case bounds are asserted against the schema's own values instead of being restated as independent literals.

Whole-stream validation applies the shared mode policy as well as the fixed budgets: normal suppresses debug task detail, including every test case, with exact ordinary elision accounting, while verbose admits it and both preserve failure priority.
Violations are ordered by path and then by code, with paths compared by code unit rather than by locale, and array indices above nine ordered numerically.
Run success is reported by the strict unified verdict, and an aborted run is a distinct status that still lists the failures it accumulated.
The sanitization helper redacts every high-confidence credential family and strips control characters while retaining member names.
